selection_rule: prefer a currently operating program whose public owner evidence can close service, distribution, or delivery gates now
prefer a candidate with a defined current-law dependency over one that first needs a new candidate identity
hold unenacted bills on named legal triggers even when their existing dossiers are comparatively mature
use fiscal scale only after operating status, owner evidence, service floors, distribution, and current-law fit
selection authorizes an evidence audit only and never admits a fiscal effect

rank_rows.shortest_active_path: reconcile the post-2025 current-law program, then test producer distribution, participation, insurer return, disaster substitution, resilience, and food-security evidence
rank_rows.ranking_reason: AGR combines an operating federal program, public administrative evidence surfaces, a defined scored option, and material scale; those facts make its evidence ceiling testable now without treating the old score as current law.

rank_rows.shortest_active_path: reconcile current appropriation and authorization, then test household energy burden, delivery, resilience, spillovers, substitution, and income-geographic incidence
rank_rows.ranking_reason: Current program and delivery evidence can improve the floor assessment now, but the selected reduction is small and lacks a matching current-law score.

rank_rows.ranking_reason: Owner data can support a current service-floor audit, but later eligibility, funding, and loan changes create a more entangled current-law dependency than AGR or SEE.
